subject: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines: maintenance windows, uptime targets, service credits
messages:
From: Emma Huang <emma.huang@edgepay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines (maintenance windows & credits)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our internal review, we've got a couple of redlines on the SLA section of the Order Form (attached: EdgePay_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf). High level asks: 

- Uptime target: asking for 99.95% (monthly) for production endpoints instead of 99.9%.
- Service credits: want linear credits starting at 99.8% with a floor of 20% of monthly fees for complete outage months; please remove any absolute cap under $X.
- Response times: severity definitions — S1 (platform down) 30 minutes initial response and 4 hours to mitigation plan; S2 4 hours initial response.
- Maintenance windows: propose a single weekly 2 hour window at UTC 03:00-05:00, with advance notice 72 hours; we need to avoid rolling maintenance that can span business hours.

Can you confirm which of these are negotiable and what trade-offs you would propose vs. price/commitment? We are targeting procurement sign-off by 05/16.

Also CCing our legal point of contact for any clause-level comments.

Thanks,
Emma Huang
Senior Procurement Manager
EdgePay Inc.

Attachment: EdgePay_SLA_Redlines_v2.pdf (PDF, 23KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Huang <emma.huang@edgepay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines (maintenance windows & credits)

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: most items are negotiable, but some need to be scoped to deployment type (hosted vs Dedicated). I've attached a redline diff with inline comments (redlines-diff.docx). Key trade-offs: 

- Uptime: We can commit to 99.95% for Dedicated instances with a 12-month reserved capacity commit. For hosted API at current tiers, 99.9% is our standard; we can offer a commercial credit to bridge to 99.95 for a higher spend tier.

- Credits: We prefer a capped monthly credit (max 100% of monthly fees) to avoid open-ended exposure. As a compromise, propose a tiered credit schedule that increases non-linearly below 99.8% (e.g., 10% @ 99.8-99.5, 30% @ 99.5-99.0, 100% @ <99.0), with a separate negotiated cap for Dedicated.

- Response times: We can accept your S1/S2 definitions but ask to make SLA clock stop for scheduled maintenance and for force majeure. For mitigation plan timing, propose 8 hours to initial mitigation plan on S1, 24 hours to full RCA for S1.

- Maintenance: We can commit to a 2-hour weekly window in the region you prefer for Dedicated; hosted customers share a global maintenance calendar — to meet your request we can provide a dedicated maintenance window if you take Dedicated or a guaranteed blackout period with 99.99% availability except scheduled windows.

Next steps: Lauren (legal) — can you review the clause-level items I flagged? Aditya — can you confirm cost delta for 99.95 SLA on Dedicated (ballpark)?

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines-diff.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Huang <emma.huang@edgepay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines (maintenance windows & credits)

Hi all,

I've taken a pass on the Order Form and MSA SLA sections. High-level legal comments attached (SLA_CLAUSE_PROPOSAL.docx). Main points: 

- Credit cap: our standard is a monthly cap equal to the monthly recurring fees. Removing any cap exposes Redwood and our hosts to unlimited liability; we can accept a higher cap for Dedicated with a reciprocal indemnity carve-out.

- Severity & response: define severity triggers with objective criteria (error codes, metrics) rather than customer subjective reports. Also request language that allows us to pause SLA clock for third-party infra outages (e.g., cloud provider).

- Maintenance scheduling: we can add an explicit clause that scheduled maintenance requires 72 hours' notice and will not count toward uptime. For the weekly 2-hour window: specify a maximum of 2 hours per calendar week and allow a single quarterly extended maintenance of up to 6 hours with notice.

- Fallback clause: recommend adding a clause that if a model variant is unavailable the system will route to a fallback model with documented performance characteristics; that should be treated as an availability event only if the fallback fails.

If EdgePay agrees to the Dedicated pricing commitment proposed by Vivek, I can accept the 99.95 obligation with the higher credit cap.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_CLAUSE_PROPOSAL.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Emma Huang <emma.huang@edgepay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, EdgePay Legal <legal@edgepay.com>
Date: 2025-05-13T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines (maintenance windows & credits)

Vivek / Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. EdgePay's procurement view: we can consider Dedicated if the pricing delta is reasonable. On credits, EdgePay cannot accept a hard cap below 50% in months with major outages; the tiered schedule you suggested is workable if the cap is increased for Dedicated customers.

A few clarifications: 
- We need the weekly maintenance window to be fixed (UTC 03:00-05:00) for our ops team; would Redwood commit to that for Dedicated?
- For response times, the business requires 4-hour mitigation for S1, not 8 — that's critical.
- Please include the fallback-model clause as Lauren suggested; also add a clause that fallback model performance degradation must be communicated to a technical contact immediately.

We're under a procurement deadline Friday 05/16. Can Redwood provide a consolidated redline and final commercial terms by end-of-day 05/14?

Best,
Emma

> On May 12, 2025, at 11:34, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> > [Vivek's initial trade-off email and redlines-diff.docx attached]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Huang <emma.huang@edgepay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - SLA redlines (maintenance windows & credits)

Emma —

Attached is a consolidated redline (Consolidated_SLA_Redlines_20250512.pdf) that reflects the agreed negotiation path: Dedicated 99.95% with a higher credit cap (up to 200% of monthly fees in defined outage scenarios), hosted baseline 99.9% with a purchase-tier add-on to reach 99.95. We accepted the fixed weekly maintenance window for Dedicated (UTC 03:00-05:00) and added explicit language for fallback-model behavior and notification. Response timing: we are keeping the S1 mitigation plan at 4 hours (per your request) but will make the RCA 24 hours after mitigation.

Action items: 
- Aditya: finalize Dedicated pricing delta and include in the Order Form (ETA EOD 05/14).
- Lauren: prepare countersigned clause set and confirm credit cap language for Dedicated.
- EdgePay: confirm acceptance or provide final redlines by 05/15 to meet procurement timeline.

I'll set up a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow 05/15 at 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite to follow. If we get final redline by EOD 05/14, legal can push to signature queue.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Consolidated_SLA_Redlines_20250512.pdf (PDF, 28KB)
